title: refactor: simplify GSoC frontend
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Shares the GSoC markdown shell used by the contributing and code-of-conduct pages.
- Centralizes repeated frontmatter parsing for FAQs, mentors, projects, and timeline entries.
- Removes unused navigation code, the React asset, navigation CSS, and dormant theme tokens.
- Keeps rendered page behavior and parser output intact.
- Net change: 14 files, 315 additions, 893 deletions.

Checks:
- `npm run build --prefix apps/gsoc`
- Parser equivalence: 18 FAQs, 3 mentors, 6 projects, 10 timeline entries
- Removed-symbol reference scan
- `git diff --check`
- GSoC lint improves from 15 existing errors on `main` to 14

gist.headline: One shell, fewer crumbs
gist.blurb: The GSoC site tidied its garden shed: shared markdown pages now do the repeated work, while old navigation and theme leftovers have gone back to the compost.
gist.summary: Refactored the GSoC frontend around a shared MarkdownDocumentPage shell and centralized frontmatter parsing for 18 FAQs, 3 mentors, 6 projects, and 10 timeline entries without changing rendered output.
gist.impact: GSoC contributors get the same pages and parser results, with 893 lines of duplicate UI, unused navigation code, React assets, CSS, and dormant theme tokens removed from the maintenance path.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy GSoC garden-shed workspace where several paper markdown pages feed neatly into one shared filing shell, while Polli helps sort duplicate scraps into a compost bin. Small code-plants and a retro terminal represent the preserved parser output and a simpler frontend structure.
